description: We’re a multidisciplinary team exploring how AI, machine learning, and data visualization can turn NASA microgravity combustion data into useful fire-safety insights. We’re looking for creative teammates interested in AI/ML, Python, data science, software development, visualization, and space exploration.
summary: Free Fall Fire Atlas is an SI-powered web dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion investigations (PSI) into fire-safety insights for a specific crew habitat. Pick a spacecraft, Moon Base or pressurized rover; the atlas ranks 20 investigations (19 matched to PSI accessions), maps their test envelopes against the habitat, plots all 129 BASS-II ISS tests from the PSI-25 experimental table, writes a cited fire-safety brief, and answers questions with Claude grounded only in the records. Key finding: every BASS-II test ran below 23% O2, and no solid-material microgravity fire data covers the 34% O2 / 8.2 psia exploration atmosphere planned for rovers.
details: Choose a habitat preset (ISS/Orion 21% O2, Moon Base 30%/10.2 psi, Pressurized Rover 34%/8.2 psi, Mars Transit, Earth) or set oxygen, pressure, airflow, gravity, fuels and safety focus. The atlas shows: a habitat-specific thesis and KPIs; an oxygen ladder of data coverage by fuel type; evidence coverage; a cited fire-safety brief with a recommended next experiment; investigations ranked 0-100 with reasons, data status, PSI accession and primary NASA source; a test-level chart of all 129 BASS-II tests (PSI-25); a heuristic similarity distance to published test envelopes; a next-generation equipment map (detection, suppression, ventilation/materials); an evidence map; side-by-side comparison; and Ask the Atlas, cited Q&A.HOW IT WORKSA structured extraction layer holds one record per investigation (fuels, geometry, O2, pressure, airflow, hardware, measurements, finding, Earth application, data status, PSI accession, source link), verified against PSI and NASA Technical Reports. A weighted relevance model scores safety-pillar fit, fuel phase and O2/airflow/pressure proximity. A serverless function sends records to Claude with rules: answer only from records, cite every claim, separate reported results from inference, name gaps.KEY FINDINGSAll 129 BASS-II tests ran at 13.6-22.2% initial O2. Saffire-IV-VI (NTRS, not in PSI) reached about 29-31% O2 at reduced pressure. ACME BRE fuels self-extinguished in still air below about 25% O2 but burned for minutes above it. No solid-material data covers 34% O2 / 8.2 psia. PSI has no partial-gravity data; lunar and Mars behavior cannot be directly extrapolated.LIMITATIONSSeveral envelopes are approximate; test-level data included for BASS-II only; the similarity distance is a heuristic, not a flammability prediction; ranking weights are expert-chosen.TOOLSHTML/CSS/JavaScript, Node.js serverless on Vercel, Anthropic Claude API, GitHub.
